answer: Under bonded escrow, correlated equivocation by \(k\) identities incurs pairwise penalties proportional to \(k(k-1)/2\), or \(O(k^2)\), rather than letting a controller dilute risk across aliases. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation: repeated losses compound, imposing an exponential multiplier on the swarm’s capital loss. A zephyr of aliases cannot shelter an orchard of claims when each coordinated timbered branch shares the evidence and cost.
